To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the flocculus is the major source of climbing fiber input to the dorsal cap, (2) the dorsal cap receives no other significant climbing fiber input, (3) flocculectomized rabbits exhibit no retrograde cell death in the dorsal cap, and (4) floccular Purkinje cell degeneration does not produce retrograde cell death or shrinkage in the dorsal cap.

surgical ablation of flocculus and chemical destruction of floccular Purkinje cells produce retrograde cell loss by 40% and 0%, respectively, in the contralaterally located dorsal cap of the inferior olive in albino rabbits.
the retrograde cell loss induced in the inferior olive by a unilateral lesion of the floccular cortex is not due to the death of the Purkinje cells of the flocculocerebellum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the retrograde influence of surgical or chemical lesions in the cerebellum on neurons of the inferior olivary complex.
the retrograde influence of cerebella cortical lesions on neurons of the inferior olivary complex in albino rabbits.
the influence of surgical and kainic acid lesions of the floccular complex upon the inferior olive in the albino rabbit.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
surgical ablation of the floccular cortex produces a retrograde cell loss, but chemical ablation does not.

surgical ablation of the floccular cortex causes a retrograde cell loss of 41% accompanied in the dorsal cap by a size reduction, while kainic acid-induced degeneration of Purkinje cells causes no cell loss in the ipsilateral dorsal cap but a slight reduction in the cell size.
surgical ablation of the cerebellar cortex induces cell loss in the contralaterally located dorsal cap.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the retrograde influence of a lesion upon the inferior olive depends upon the extent to which the lesioned area is innervated by climbing fibers.
a surgical lesion of the floccular cortex is a more powerful retrograde influence upon the inferior olive than is a chemical lesion.

a lesion of the cerebellar cortex, whether surgical or chemical, produces a cell loss by retrograde transsynaptic degeneration only in the inferior olive when the lesion is made in the cerebellar flocculus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cerebellum has a significant retrograde influence upon the inferior olive, but that this influence is dependent upon the type of injury.
the cerebellar cortical lesion induced a cell loss in the ipsilateral dorsal cap.
the flocculus exerts an important influence upon the development and maintenance of neurons in the dorsal cap of the inferior olive.
